passage:
Naveen: Everyone in class got the new phone. I'm the only one with the cracked old one 😔
Ramesh: Who cares? Mine is older
Naveen: You don't care. I do. Kabir held his up in front of everyone and then looked at mine
Ramesh: Did you ask your dad?
Naveen: He'd just say we can't. I didn't want to hear it
Ramesh: Does yours still work for school?
Naveen: ...yes. It works. It's just embarrassing
Ramesh: Then that's a want, not a need. Tell him that. And say what you'd save toward
Naveen: Ok. Tonight I'll tell Papa I'd like to save for a better one over a year and ask what he thinks
Ramesh: Deal 🙂

qa.q: Who held up a new phone in front of everyone?
qa.a: Kabir held up the new phone in front of everyone.

qa.q: What is Naveen feeling about the cracked old phone?
qa.a: Naveen feels embarrassed and left out, since everyone else has the new one and Kabir looked at Naveen's cracked phone.

qa.q: What choice did Naveen make after Ramesh's questions?
qa.a: Naveen decided to tell Papa that the old phone works, admit it is a want, and offer to save toward a better one over a year.

qa.q: How might Papa see Naveen's request?
qa.a: Papa may appreciate hearing an honest want with a plan to save, rather than a demand, though the passage does not show Papa's reply.

grounding: A teenager wants the same phone as peers and feels embarrassed, and talking about needs, wants and choices builds resilience.

passage:
Before sports day, Zubin stood at the school gate looking at his classmates' shiny new running shoes, then at his own canvas ones with a patch on the toe. His ears went hot. That evening at the vegetable stall behind the bus stand, his mother Jyoti was counting change. "You've been quiet."
"Everyone has good shoes."
She did not say "be grateful." She said, "Which ones would you need to run, and which would you only want to be seen in?"
Zubin thought. "To run I need a grip and no holes."
On Sunday at the weekly market they found a plain pair with a good sole. Sports day, Zubin ran the 200 metres and came second. His shoes weren't the shiniest. He noticed he didn't care.

qa.q: Where was Zubin's mother Jyoti counting change?
qa.a: She was counting change at the vegetable stall behind the bus stand.

qa.q: What was Zubin feeling at the school gate?
qa.a: He felt embarrassed about his patched canvas shoes, as shown by his hot ears.

qa.q: What question from Jyoti helped Zubin choose wisely?
qa.a: She asked which shoes he would need to run and which he would only want to be seen in, so he separated a need from a want and chose a plain pair with a good sole.

qa.q: How does Jyoti respond to Zubin's complaint that everyone has good shoes?
qa.a: She does not lecture him to be grateful. She asks a question and lets him think, showing she takes his feelings seriously.

grounding: A teenager feels embarrassed by a modest family next to peers, and talking about needs, wants and choices builds resilience against status pressure.
